title.narrative: Chad COVID-19 Strategic Preparedness and Response Project

description.narrative: To prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness in Chad.

While the project will help strengthen the national capacity to respond to the COVID-19 emergency, the distribution of equipment and supplies and the training of staff will prioritize the seven provinces identified by the WHO as high-risk provinces. These provinces are those were there are points of entry to the country and include: N’Djamena, Lake Chad, Mayo Kebbi East, Mayo Kebbi West, Logone Oriental, Moyen-Chari and Ouaddai.The project has 4 components: (1) Emergency COVID-19 Preparedness and Response, (2) Community Engagement and Social and Behavior Change Communication, (3) Implementation Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Coordination, and (4) Contingent Emergency Response (CERC).

condition.narrative: As agreed in the ESCP, the MWMP of the parent project is being revised and will be published no later than three months after theEffective Date.
As agreed in the ESCP, the Security Risk Evaluation (SRE) will be prepared, adopted, and disclosed no later than three months afterthe Effective Date.

Not later than 30 days after the Effective Date (or such later date as agreed to by the Association), the Recipient, through theMoPHNS, shall: (a) update in form and manner acceptable to the Association the manual Project Implementation Manual (“PIM”); and(b) thereafter, continue to implement the Project in accordance with the updated PIM. Except as the Association shall otherwiseagree, the Recipient shall not amend or waive the PIM. In case of any conflict between the provisions of the PIM and the provisionsof this Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement shall prevail.

Not later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, the Recipient, through the MPHP, shall: (a) update and adopt theProject Implementation Manual in a manner acceptable to the Association (“Project Implementation Manual” or “PIM”)
Not later than two months after the Effective Date, hire an environmental specialist, and a gender-based violence specialist andthereafter maintain these positions throughout Project implementation.
Per ESCP the project's grievance mechanism shall be operational not later than 30 days after the project's effective date.

Schedule 2, section 1 (B): Not later than 30 days after the Effective Date (or such later date as agreed to by the Association),the Recipient, through the MoH, shall: (a) prepare and adopt a manual acceptable to the Association (“Project ImplementationManual” or “PIM”); and (b) thereafter, implement the Project in accordance with the PIM. Except as the Association shall otherwiseagree, the Recipient shall not amend or waive the PIM.

Schedule 2, section 1, D.7: The Recipient shall recruit an environmental specialist and social specialist for the PIU before thecommencement of Project activities with potential social or environmental impacts, and shall thereafter ensure that saidspecialists be retained throughout Project implementation.
The Project's updated GM shall be operational not later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date. It shall be maintained andadequately resourced throughout Project implementation.

The Recipient shall, not later than forty-five (45) days after the Effective Date, and thereafter, on November 30 of the samecalendar year for the remaining period of Project implementation, prepare and furnish to the Association, a program of Projectactivities proposed for implementation in the following calendar year, including: (a) a detailed timetable for the sequencing andimplementation of said activities; and (b) the types of expenditures required for such activities, a proposed financing plan and abudget (“Annual Work Program”).

title.narrative: 2.1. Communication campaigns about COVID-19 broadcasted to communities

comment.narrative:
This activity was completed under UNICEF Contract. The collective"Les Stars Amis des Enfants"; developed a song and a video clip on social and "physical distancing, which were broadcast on Chadian television channels TV Tchad, Electron TV, Toumaï TV, Tchad 24, national radio, private radio stations and social networks. These songs helped raise awareness among 2,994,886 people across the 14 provinces"
Twenty (20) web concerts and three (3) other clips on different themes related to COVID-19 (social distancing, stigmatization of people with COVID-19, domestic violence and violence against children during confinement, etc.) were produced by the "Stars friends of children" collective, and broadcasted on the different digital platforms and social networks of UNICEF.

title.narrative: 1.2. Healthcare workers trained on surveillance and investigation

comment.narrative: This training process has been conducted under WHO contract. The target was to train 250 health workers on surveillance and investigation. The project trained 317 members of surveillance teams and 208 staff at points of entry, i.e. a total of 525 workers.

title.narrative: 1.1. Update of National COVID-19 Response Action Plan

comment.narrative: A National Vaccine Deployment Plan has been developed as part of the COVID-19 response and was updated.

title.narrative: 2.2. National COVID-19 risk communication and community engagement strategy established

comment.narrative: Communication strategy document drawn up by the “Coordination National de Riposte Sanitaire”(CNRS) at Covid-19 under the lead of the MoH Communication Department

title.narrative: 1.3. Health workers trained on case definition, management, infection prevention and control for COVID-19

comment.narrative: This training process has been conducted under WHO contract. The project trained 521 staff on case definition and management, 129 on severe COVID-19 treatment, and 864 on infection prevention and control. There is no current plan to increase the number of staff trained.

title.narrative: Targeted healthcare facilities providing COVID-19 treatment with isolation capacity

comment.narrative: All 08 hospitals in priority provinces designated within priority intervention area for Integrated Case Management have isolation capacity including Farcha and Renaissance Hospitals in N’Djamena . In most cases this means separated wings/rooms for the treatment of COVID-19 patients.

title.narrative: 1.4. Eligible households provided with food and basic supplies within quarantined populations

comment.narrative: The price reduction for rice bag by the government's decision to exempt this product reached more eligible households than expected.

title.narrative: 3.1. Technical crisis coordination meetings issuing an official report on epidemic surveillance and response

comment.narrative: National Coordination Committee meetings have been held twice a week and the reports of these meetings have been disseminated widely.

title.narrative: Designated laboratories with COVID-19 functioning diagnostic equipment, test kits, and reagents per MPHNS guidelines

comment.narrative: As part of the laboratory strengthening strategy, the Government of Chad, with the support of multiple partners, has equipped 24 laboratories (11 in the priority provinces) and they are functioning and performing COVID-19 tests.
